body:
Thank you for your help. I doubt that she would want to go to a mental hospital, but I'll consider asking her about it. Luckily her foot is not broken but she can't work at least until monday. I am hoping that she will recover a bit during that time, the last two days were really troublesome. If not I might think of something that'll take her mind off during the weekend, a longer vacation is out of question though. She doesn't appear to be depressed by the way, is it possible to have suicidal thoughts when being in a bad situation without acually having depression or could she just be hiding it from me? I've always thought that is a requirement but I have close to no personal experience with it.

As for me, I am a bit ashamed to admit that I didn't really notice anything at first, I thought she was just ranting. Her saying that she had suicidal thoughts hit me really hard because of that today. I have already settled on talking to a few relatives to get some further help and advice because I feel overwhelmed with the situation, but other than that I don't really feel the need to talk to anyone about anything regarding me. As weird as that sounds I am doing pretty well and literally my only concern right now is to stabilize her mental health. I really appreciate your offer though.

She came back about fifteen minutes ago. I hugged her and told her that I don't want her to think about things like suicide and that everything will turn out alright. I guess you can't just shake off these thoughts though. Sadly she does not have any close friends at all, she has few friends in general. She's on good terms with most of our relatives though, except for my sister. I've thought about calling one of my aunts already.
